predecessors.name: Balinese Kingdom (Gelgel)
predecessors.text: Bali, from the Gelgel kingdom that 'began to break up' after 1651

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: all of Bali under 'the total rule of the Dutch over Bali' after the 1908 assault on Klungkung

ledger.x: 1686-1687: the Gelgel kingdom gives way to the Nine Kingdoms of Bali.
1846: the first Dutch military expedition against north Bali.
1849: the third expedition ends the contest for the north coast, the king of Buleleng and his retinue dying in a puputan.
1849: the Dutch take Buleleng and Jembrana.
1906: the Dutch destroy the Badung royal house.
1908: the Dutch assault on Klungkung ends Balinese rule.
1908: the Nine Kingdoms end with the fall of Klungkung and Bali becomes Dutch; Cliopatria ends the row in 1907.

wars.name: Dutch expeditions against Buleleng
wars.outcome: The Dutch, helped by Bangli in 1849, defeat Buleleng and take Buleleng and Jembrana; the king of Buleleng and his retinue die in a puputan.

wars.name: Balinese expedition to Blambangan (1814)
wars.outcome: The page gives no result; it records only the clash.

wars.name: Dutch intervention in Lombok and Karangasem (1894)
wars.outcome: The Dutch defeat the Balinese ruler of Lombok, 'adding both Lombok and Karangasem to their possessions'.

wars.name: Dutch intervention in Bali (1906)
wars.outcome: The Dutch eliminate the Badung royal house in a puputan; about 1,000 die.

wars.name: Dutch intervention in Bali (1908)
wars.outcome: A mass suicide at Klungkung ends the dynasty and establishes the total rule of the Dutch over Bali.

certainty.note: The island coast is natural, but the borders between the nine kingdoms and the Balinese holdings on Lombok and in Blambangan are not on the pages.
The cuts of 1849 (Buleleng, Jembrana), 1894 (Karangasem) and 1906 (Badung) follow kingdom lands whose borders the pages do not give.
